CO5300 narrow-window kernel FIT used for the final physical test
inputs.revision: CO5300 driver from OS fd92a74af9e5ced92b5942b19c14b9929c5a6941, RAM boot with the R5 LittleFS root on NOR

scenario: Build the original QML and present its centered 400 × 400 scene on wsdisplay. Tap the red square, wait one second, then tap it at its new position.
expected: Each tap moves the red square to the right by 50 pixels over 1000 milliseconds.
observed: On the original R5 kernel, the operator saw the square move after tapping it and reported visible judder. After region rendering and the CO5300 update, the operator repeated the test and reported noticeably smoother motion with no visible jerks. The running application recorded three physical press/release pairs in this final session. The latest driver transfer covered 102 columns starting at x=188 across two rows. The driver reported zero transfer errors.
limits: The original physical trace recorded 25 distinct drawn x coordinates including endpoints per 50-pixel move, without frame timestamps. The Qt Quick 6.12 host reference checks the intermediate positions and endpoints.

Separate full-scene and region benchmark runs each replayed three scripted taps on the physical display. Each reported time is the mean userspace wsdisplay presentation call for one move. On the original kernel, full rendering produced 28 distinct application positions per move and region rendering produced 27, 30 and 30. On the RAM kernel, the counts were 20, 19 and 20 for full rendering and 23, 26 and 26 for region rendering.
The panel driver counts successful rows. Physical smoothness was assessed by the operator. Optical frame rate and touch-to-photon latency were not measured.
Only the running RAM kernel included the CO5300 changes during acceptance. The normal NOR boot still selected the previous kernel.
